title: Clocks
summary: A clock is a 60-minute template of an hour on air. It is a set of playlists and timed inserts; the system lays out the hour from them by itself. The grid decides which clock plays in which hour.

entities.text: The playlists the hour is built from, of any type, for example "Music" and "Jingles". You do not list single tracks: the system chooses them.

Each playlist says how it is placed: Fill (fills the time left), Spread N (N tracks spread over the hour), Start, End, Start and end, or Middle (a track starting at about 30:00, from 25:00 to 35:00). The rule is set on the playlist page.
A clock may override the rule of a playlist for itself, for example "Jingles" spread 4 times in a morning clock instead of 2. The playlist and other clocks keep their rule.

A clock needs at least one fill playlist. With several, give each a share: "New releases" 30 and "Gold" 70 means about three music tracks in ten come from "New releases". Give every fill playlist a share, or none; without shares every fill playlist has the same chance, however many tracks it has.

A track, or a track drawn from a playlist, at a time of the hour with seconds, for example 29:40. It plays in every hour of the clock. Inserts close together play back to back without music between them.
How far an insert may start before or after its time, ±1 minute by default. An insert at 30:00 may begin anywhere from 29:00 to 31:00, so the music before it can end naturally.

Saving builds one hour with the real library and play history and shows it: every track with its start, length, and where it came from. Planned hours may choose other tracks; the sample shows a typical layout.

usage: Add the playlists the hour is made of, check their rules, add timed inserts for news or station IDs, and save. Tracks of any length are used: before an insert or the end of the hour the system picks the track that fits the time left, or cuts the last one with a short fade-out. Warnings never block the save.
steps: Click Add clock and enter a name.
Add a fill playlist, for example "Music", and the other playlists, for example "Jingles".
Turn on "Own rule in this clock" for a playlist that should behave differently here.
With several fill playlists, give each a share, or leave all shares empty.
Add timed inserts, for example a jingle at 29:40 and the news playlist at 30:00.
Save, then read the sample hour and the warnings.
Assign the clock to hours on the Grid page.
mistakes: No fill playlist: every playlist has a rule such as Spread or Start, so nothing fills the hour. Add a playlist with the rule Fill.
A share on some fill playlists only. Give every fill playlist a share, or none.
Inserts too close together: an insert cannot start inside its window because the one before it runs past it. Move it later or widen its tolerance.
A fill playlist without a minimum interval in its play rules. Its tracks may repeat within the hour; attach a rule such as "Music rotation".
A rule playlist whose tracks are all blocked by play rules in some hours. That rule track is skipped, and the music covers its time.

example.title: A music hour with news at half past
example.text: Playlists: "Music" (Fill), "Jingles" (its own rule: Spread 2). Inserts: 29:40 the jingle "News intro", 30:00 the playlist "News", 30:00 tolerance ±1 minute. Saving shows an hour of music with two jingles apart from each other; the music before 29:40 ends inside the window or fades out, and the news follows the jingle without a gap.

operations.create: Saving builds the sample hour first. Problems are shown at once, not at air time.
operations.edit: Only planned hours that have not started are rebuilt, around their one-time inserts. Hours on air keep their plan.
operations.delete: A clock used in the grid or with play history cannot be deleted. Remove it from the grid first.

name.label: Name
name.text: A name you will recognize in the grid, for example "Weekday morning".

playlists.label: Add a playlist
playlists.text: Adds a playlist of any type to the clock. Each playlist can be in a clock once.

override.label: Own rule in this clock
override.text: Off: the playlist's own placement rule applies. On: choose the rule this clock uses for it.

clock_rule.label: Placement in clocks
clock_rule.text: Fill, Spread, Start, End, Start and end, or Middle. See the terms above.

clock_count.label: Tracks per hour
clock_count.text: For Spread only: how many tracks of the playlist play in the hour, 1 to 12.

fill_weight.label: Share
fill_weight.text: For fill playlists only: a relative share from 1 to 100. The page shows each share in percent of all shares.

offset_ms.label: Time
offset_ms.text: When the insert starts, as mm:ss from 00:00 to 59:59. The arrow keys move it by a second; with Shift, or Page Up and Page Down, by a minute.

tolerance_ms.label: Start tolerance
tolerance_ms.text: How many seconds the insert may start before or after its time, 0 to 600. A new insert proposes the default from the settings.

track_id.label: Track
track_id.text: The track the insert plays every hour. Use the play button to listen to it.

playlist_id.label: Playlist
playlist_id.text: A track of this playlist is chosen for every hour, following its play rules.
